_purpose: ONE source of truth for the connections payload, sitting between the Python that
EMITS it and the JavaScript that RENDERS it. Before this file the JS tests froze the
payload by hand, so a server-side key rename kept them green while the real options-page
map and the real popup panel broke.
Both ends are held to it:
* tests/unit/test_connections_contract.py calls the REAL get_connections_info() and
asserts its output conforms -> a Python rename fails there.
* tests/js/options-map.test.mjs and tests/js/popup.test.mjs validate their hand-written
fixtures against this file (tests/js/contract.mjs) -> a contract updated without the
Renaming a key therefore costs three edits (emitter, contract, fixtures) and cannot be
_consumers: extension-gecko/options.js  - the Health tab's connection map (renderConnectionMap et al.)

_types.int: Python int (never bool) / JS integral number
_types.number: Python int|float / JS number - used where int-vs-float is not load-bearing
_types.null: Python None / JS null (an ABSENT key is not the same thing - see `optional`)

_schema.required: key -> allowed types. The key MUST be present. Absence is a contract breach.
_schema.optional: key -> allowed types. May be absent; when present it must type-check, and its name is a known key (so a fixture carrying it is not carrying a typo).
_schema.of: for an array key: every element must conform to the named object.
_schema.discriminator: for a heterogeneous array: the key whose value picks the element's object.

payload._comment: The dict get_connections_info() returns. `requester_slot` is NOT one of its keys: server.py's `server.get_connections` WS relay (~:1403) grafts it on afterwards, and the options page's /health fallback synthesizes it as null. So it is optional here and the Python test asserts the emitter does NOT invent it.

server_row._comment: The server process's own row (kind='server'). `version` is shared-py/browserplug_shared/version.py - the SAME number the launcher reports and both manifests carry (parity invariant H).

extension_row._comment: One row per CONNECTED browser (kind='extension'). `slot` - not `pid` - correlates it with its extension_instance: a REMOTE browser has no pid. `engine`/`platform`/`browser_info` are what the browser said about ITSELF in its hello, and for a remote one they are the only identification there is - no pid, no exe path, no start time - so the popup prints them in the row's tooltip and in its copied block. `browser_info` is passed through whole (a gecko fork's identity hides in a key of its own); `version` is the EXTENSION's build, not the browser's, which lives in browser_info.version. All four are null on a browser that never sent them.

mcp_client_row._comment: One row per MCP client PROCESS (kind='mcp_client'); its sessions are collapsed into `sessions`. `launcher_pid` is the stdio proxy between it and the server (null = a direct HTTP client, e.g. GitLab Duo) - the map draws it as its own hop. `launcher_version` is what that process reports on its /health poll; null means it never did, i.e. a launcher older than version reporting. provider/model come from the Kilo CLI, pi and GitHub Copilot Chat detectors and are best-effort: absent on any miss. `copilot` is the Copilot Chat detector's whole answer (see copilot_session); on those rows `cwd` and `label` name the window's workspace instead of the VS Code install dir. `target_browser_slot` is the browser this client's tool calls are routed to right now (null = nothing connected, or its selection points at a departed browser, in which case its calls error rather than route elsewhere); `target_browser_explicit` says whether that was a browsers(action='use') choice or just the default - the connection map draws the routing line from them. `cmdline` is the process's argv with secret-looking values masked (server.py :: _sanitized_cmdline), the field the popup's copied row leans on to identify a client running under a generic interpreter: exe_path for any node CLI is just node.exe. null when psutil could not read it. `vendor` is who ships the client (server.py :: _CLIENT_VENDORS), keyed on `friendly`; null for any client we could not name, which is why the popup prints it as an extra fact rather than laying the row out around it.

copilot_session._comment: GitHub Copilot Chat rows only (server/usage_panels/copilot_data.py :: detect_session), under the same kilo_details gate as provider/model. Every key is always present; all but `requests` may be null. `requests` counts the window's successful chat requests in the log tail; `chat_title`/`chat_turns` come from the Copilot session matched to this window; `workspace` is that session's cwd, else the folder the extension host's children run in.

command._comment: `params` is _format_args()'s compact dict; the JS renders it verbatim and tolerates a string.

extension_instance._comment: The browser registry, one entry per known browser (connected or not - see currently_connected). `last_activity_epoch` counts REAL browser commands only, so the map does not light an edge on its own polling. `version` is the EXTENSION's (manifest.json); everything else describes the BROWSER - the map draws the two as separate boxes. windows/tabs/active_tabs/loaded_tabs/state_hms come from the extension's browser_state pushes: null until the first one lands (or on an extension too old to send them). `active_tab_list` is one {id, title, last_hms} entry per window's foreground tab (last_hms is on the BROWSER's clock, null when nothing is known about that tab); [] means 'none', null means 'this extension never said'. The OPTIONAL keys are connection forensics, added in 1.8.8 (`encrypted` in 1.9: the socket carries only sealed records) and optional so the hand-written JS fixtures do not each have to carry them: last_disconnect_hms/last_close_code/last_close_reason describe the PREVIOUS drop and survive the reconnect that replaced it; hello_latency_ms is socket accept -> valid hello; reported_journal is the extension's own [{t,e,code?,reason?,attempt?}] account of what happened while it was away (server/ws/connection_log.py), which is the only artifact that survives a browser being killed.

last_command._comment: _last_command_info(). Two shapes, one key set: the newest MCP call's WS-level record, OR - when that call never touched a browser (browsers, server_info) - the call record itself with action/ack null. browser_slot/launcher_pid/timings are attached ONLY when the timing record matches this command (_attach_call_timings), hence optional.

outcome._comment: The structured verdict for THIS call, written by ToolOutcomeMiddleware via mcp_tools._record_outcome. The agent learns a call failed from the MCP isError flag, but an MCP error result carries no _meta - so an operator/monitor can only learn it here. null when no tool call has completed yet. failed=false with a non-empty degraded list is a SUCCESS that returned less than it was asked for (truncated, empty extraction, unsettled).

timings._comment: The per-hop breakdown the map replays. `started_epoch` is the replay-once key. A leg that did not happen is null - never 0.
